newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TIMELINES - Today in History - April 23.
newsitem.headline: TIMELINES - Today in History - April 23.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Australia's first female University graduate BELLA GUERIN was born in 1858. She received her Bachelor of Arts degree from Melbourne University in 1883. A well known radical she accused Labor Party members of "using women as performing poodles and packhorses".
Australian teacher and poet KATE BAKER was born in 1861. She became famous for publishing JOSEPH FURPHY's book "Such is Life".
Russian composer SERGEI PROKOFIEV was born in 1891. His most famous work was "Peter and the Wolf".
Canadian statesman LESTER PEARSON was born in 1897. He received a Nobel Peace prize in 1957 for his solution to the Suez crisis.
SHIRLEY TEMPLE BLACK, American child actress was born in 1928. Famous for her curly blonde locks, she eventually left acting and became America's Ambassador to Ghana.

American singer ROY ORBISON was born in 1936. With his trademark dark sunglasses and black clothes he had a massive hit with "Only the Lonely". Another of his songs "Pretty Woman" was a hit in its own right, then shot up the charts all over again with the release of the movie of the same name.
US singer RAY PETERSON was born in 1939. He had hits with "Tell Laura I Love Her"(1960) and "Corinna, Corinna" (1960).
British lead guitarist with 'Def Leppard' STEVE CLARKE was born in 1960.
** EVENTS **
1014 : High King of Ireland BRIAN BORU was killed
repelling Viking invaders at the battle of Clontarf.
1616 : The artistic world suffered two great losses.

WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE died aged 52 at his home in Stratford-upon-Avon, upon his birthday. Originally an actor he became famous for his numerous plays and poems which weren't fully published until after his death. However many of his plays were performed during his lifetime. Considered probably the greatest writer in English literature, many of his plays were originally intended for the masses. The other great loss was Spanish writer MIGUEL de CERVANTES who wrote "Don Quixote".
1661 : CHARLES II was crowned King of England.
1791 : French nobleman Count DONATIEN ALPHONSE FRANCOIS
de SADE published a controversial novel which claimed pain could bring sexual pleasure. Later to become the Marquis de SADE, his novel and his name were combined to create the term sadist.
1795 : WARREN HASTINGS was acquitted of high treason and
all crimes allegedly commited during his term as governor-general in Bengal.
1838 : Explorer JOHN MCDOUGALL STUART arrived in the
centre of Australia.
1850 : English poet WILLIAM WORDSWORTH died at the age of
1915 : RUPERT BROOKE, British First World War poet, died
of blood poisoning off Skiros, Greece.
1935 : STALIN opened the Moscow underground, the largest
underground railway system in the world.
1945 : Field Marshall GOERING sent a telegram to HITLER,
besieged in Berlin, proposing he take control as HITLER's deputy. HITLER ordered his immediate arrest.
1949 : BILLY HUGHES broke the parliamentary service
record. He'd chalked up 54 years, eight months and six days, eclipsing the record of the late DAVID LLOYD GEORGE.
1955 : The Prime Minister BOB MENZIES opened the first
stage of the Snowy Mountain hydro-electricity scheme - the Guthega power station.
1959 : The Reserve Bank was formed to take over the
central banking function from the Commonwealth bank.
1962 : The biggest ever "Ban the Bomb" demonstration took
place in London involving 150,000 people.
1969 : SIRHAN B. SIRHAM, the man who killed ROBERT
KENNEDY was sentenced to death by a Los Angeles jury. He joined 80 other men waiting for the gas chamber on death row.
1972 : Quiz king BARRY JONES was chosen to stand for the
safe Labor seat of Melbourne at the next State election. Two months later he was elected to the House of Representatives.
1986 : OTTO PREMINGER, Austrian born film director, died;
his films included "Laura", "Carmen Jones" and "Exodus".
1990 : PAULETTE GODDARD, U.S. film actress and former
wife of Charlie Chaplin, died. She appeared with him in "Modern Times" and "The Great Dictator".
1990 : American Professor ROBERT POLHILL was released by
Lebanese kidnappers after 39 months in captivity.
1992 : SATYAJIT RAY, Indian film director best known for
"Pather Panchali", died only three weeks after being awarded a lifetime achievement Oscar. Best known for his "Pather Panchali"
1996 : Former Australian Labor prime minister PAUL
KEATING resigned from parliament, ending a political career of 27 years.
